notes.title: Start here: five classes for books, borrowers and loans
notes.body:
This is a small library tracker for the terminal, in plain Java 17. You add books and borrowers, check books out and in, and save everything to two text files in a `data` folder.

The code is split by job:

1. **model/Book.java** and **model/Borrower.java** - the nouns. A book also carries its loan state.
2. **service/LibraryManager.java** - the rules: ids, lookups, checkout and return.
3. **App.java** - the numbered menu, input parsing and display text.
4. **storage/FileStorage.java** - reading and writing the two files.

docs/onboarding/01-reading-order.md suggests reading in that order: vocabulary, then rules, then flow, then storage. The README has a section for every method; use it as a map and confirm each line in the code.

Compile with the javac line in the README and run `java -cp out librarytracker.App` in a scratch folder. Many questions in this quest are about edge cases, so try them: odd ids, odd dates, a hand-edited file.

excerpts.quote: Read it in layers so you learn the vocabulary first, then the rules, then the runtime flow.

readMore.why: One short entry per method; read each beside the method it describes.
The four reading stages and what to learn at each one.

notes.title: Concept: a loan is four fields on a Book
notes.body:
There is no Loan class. A loan is the combination of four fields on `Book`: a flag saying it is out, the id of who has it, the day it went out, and the day it is due. The book points at its borrower by **id**, and `LibraryManager` turns that id back into a `Borrower` when the display needs a name.

When fields that belong together live side by side, the interesting questions are about the moments they change. Read `Book.checkOut`, `Book.returnBook` and `Book.isOverdue`, then `LibraryManager.checkOutBook` and `returnBook`, and answer from the code:

- Which conditions does `checkOutBook` test, and in what order? What does it return at each one?
- Which of the four fields comes from the user and which from the clock?
- Does any check look at the due date itself, or at how many books a borrower holds?
- Read the comparison inside `isOverdue` carefully. Which `LocalDate` method does it use, and what does that method return when both dates are equal?
- In `App.buildBookStatus`, which parts of the status line are optional, and what decides each one?

excerpts.quote: A `Book` does not store the full `Borrower` object.

readMore.why: The loan fields and the three methods that change or read them.
The checkout and return flows written out step by step.

notes.title: Concept: two record files and when they are written
notes.body:
Data lives in `data/books.txt` and `data/borrowers.txt`. Each record is a run of `key=value` lines ending with a `---` line; the README shows a complete book record.

`FileStorage.readRecords` turns a file into a list of maps, one map per record, and `loadBooks` / `loadBorrowers` turn each map into an object. Read those three methods and note:

- What `getOrDefault` supplies when a key is missing, for each field.
- Which conversions (`Long.parseLong`, `LocalDate.parse`, `Boolean.parseBoolean`) can throw, and what kind of exception each one throws. Then look at what `App.main` catches.
- What `readRecords` does with blank lines and with a line that has no `=`.

Then look at the other direction. Find every caller of `LibraryManager.saveData`, then list every way the menu loop can end, including an exception thrown by the `Scanner`, and decide which of those paths reach a save. Finally, read `FileStorage.load` and `save` and note which directory and file operations each one performs.

excerpts.quote: The saved files use a simple record format:
id=0 title=Clean Code author=Robert C. Martin

notes.title: Why the first book gets ID 0
notes.body:
`findNextBookId` starts from `highestId = -1`, raises it to the highest id among the loaded books, and returns `highestId + 1`. With no books the loop never runs, so it returns **0**, and `addBook` hands out `nextBookId++`. Running the app on an empty folder prints "Book added with ID 0." Borrowers work the same way.

- *ID 1, counters start at one*: the starting value is -1, not 0, so the first id is 0.
- *List size plus one*: the code never looks at the list size; it looks at the highest id.
- *No ID until saved*: the id is assigned in memory when the book is created and printed right away.

excerpts.quote: long highestId = -1;
Book book = new Book(nextBookId++, title, author, emptyToNull(isbn));

readMore.why: The checklist entry that reproduced ids starting at 0.

notes.title: Why a borrower can hold any number of books
notes.body:
`checkOutBook` makes exactly three checks, each returning a message on failure: the book exists, the borrower exists, and this book is not already checked out. None of them counts how many books the borrower already has or looks at their due dates. A second available book therefore **checks out successfully**.

- *Refused because she already has a book*: no such message or rule exists in `LibraryManager`.
- *Refused until the first is returned*: same reason; returns are never consulted during checkout.
- *Only if nothing is overdue*: `isOverdue` is only used for display in `buildBookStatus`, never in a rule.

excerpts.quote: if (book.isCheckedOut()) { return "Book is already checked out."; }

notes.title: Why the borrower error wins over the checked-out error
notes.body:
`checkOutBook` runs its checks in a fixed order and returns at the first failure: book exists, then borrower exists, then book not already out. Book 0 exists, so the first check passes. Borrower 9 does not exist, so the method returns **"Borrower not found."** before it ever looks at the book's state.

- *"Book is already checked out."*: that check is third, so it is never reached here.
- *"Book not found."*: `findBookById` matches on id only; a checked-out book is still found.
- *Both messages*: each check ends the method with `return`, so only one message can come back.

excerpts.quote: Optional<Borrower> borrowerOptional = findBorrowerById(borrowerId); if (borrowerOptional.isEmpty()) { return "Borrower not found."; }

notes.title: Why a due date in the past is accepted
notes.body:
`readOptionalDate` only cares whether `LocalDate.parse` accepts the text; `2000-01-01` is a valid date, so it is returned. `checkOutBook` passes it straight to `book.checkOut` with no comparison against today. On the next listing `isOverdue` sees a due date before today and the status gets **(OVERDUE)**. The review checklist reproduced this exact case.

- *Asks for a future date*: nothing in the code compares the entered date with today.
- *Format error*: the format message appears only when parsing throws, and this date parses.
- *Only from the next day on*: the due date is already before today, so the mark appears at once.

excerpts.quote: try { return LocalDate.parse(input);
book.checkOut(borrowerId, LocalDate.now(), dueDate);

readMore.why: The checklist entry for back-dated due dates, with a goal for fixing it.

notes.title: Why a book due today is not overdue yet
notes.body:
`isOverdue` is `checkedOut && dueDate != null && dueDate.isBefore(today)`. `isBefore` is a strict comparison: a date is not before itself. So on the due date the book shows as checked out with its due date and **no (OVERDUE) mark**; the mark appears from the next day.

- *(OVERDUE) on the due date*: that would need `!dueDate.isAfter(today)`, which is not what the code says.
- *Late from midnight*: `LocalDate` has no time of day; only whole dates are compared.
- *Available*: nothing returns a book automatically; only option 6 calls `returnBook`.

excerpts.quote: return checkedOut && dueDate != null && dueDate.isBefore(today);

notes.title: What a blank due date means for a loan
notes.body:
For blank input `readOptionalDate` returns `null`, and `checkOut` stores that `null` like any other value. The loan is real (`checkedOut` is true, borrower and checkout date are set) but has **no due date**. Because `isOverdue` requires `dueDate != null`, this loan is never flagged, and `saveBooks` writes `dueDate=` with an empty value.

- *14 days by default*: no default loan length exists anywhere in the code.
- *Due on the checkout date*: the checkout date is a separate field; nothing copies it into the due date.
- *Checkout cancelled*: the prompt says "optional", and a blank answer is a valid answer.

excerpts.quote: if (input.isEmpty()) { return null; }
return checkedOut && dueDate != null && dueDate.isBefore(today);

notes.title: Why ending input loses unsaved changes here
notes.body:
When input ends, `readInt` calls `scanner.nextLine()`, which throws `NoSuchElementException`. `run()` is a plain `while` loop with no `try`/`finally`, and `main` only catches `IOException`, so the exception ends the program at once. Data reaches disk only through `saveData`, which is called by option 8 and by `exitApplication` (option 9). The new book was **never written**.

- *addBook writes the file*: `addBook` only adds to the in-memory list.
- *A finally block saves*: `run()` has no `try`/`finally` at all.
- *Saves whenever lists change*: `LibraryManager` writes only inside `saveData`.

notes.title: Why one bad date crashes startup
notes.body:
`loadBooks` passes the saved `dueDate` text to `parseDateOrNull`, which calls `LocalDate.parse`. The text `15-10-2026` is not ISO format, so it throws `DateTimeParseException`. That is an unchecked exception, not an `IOException`. `main` only has `catch (IOException e)`, so the friendly message is skipped and the JVM prints a **stack trace** and exits.

- *"Could not load library data:"*: that line only runs for an `IOException`.
- *Loads with no due date*: only a blank value becomes `null`; a malformed one throws.
- *Skipped with a warning*: no code catches errors per record.

notes.title: Why a record with no id becomes a second ID 0
notes.body:
`loadBooks` reads every field with `record.getOrDefault(key, default)`. For the id the default is the text "0", which parses fine, so a record with no `id=` line becomes a book with **ID 0**. Nothing checks for duplicates, so it sits beside the real book 0, and `findBookById(0)` will only ever return the first one in the list.

- *NumberFormatException*: "0" is a valid number; only a non-numeric id would throw.
- *Skipped as required*: the loader has no required fields at all.
- *Next free id*: ids come only from the file; `findNextBookId` runs after loading and only affects new books.

notes.title: How a loan to a missing borrower is shown
notes.body:
`buildBookStatus` starts with "Checked out" for any checked-out book. It asks `findBorrowerForBook` for the borrower, which returns `Optional.empty()` when no borrower has that id, and appends " to " plus the name only inside `ifPresent`. The checkout date and due date are appended independently. So the line reads **Checked out on (date), due (date)** with no name.

- *Available*: the book is still `checkedOut`; loading never compares the two files.
- *To Unknown*: there is no placeholder name; the name part is simply skipped.
- *Startup stops*: ids are stored as plain numbers and only resolved when something is displayed.

excerpts.quote: borrower.ifPresent(value -> builder.append(" to ").append(value.getName()));

notes.title: What a return leaves in the saved record
notes.body:
`Book.returnBook` sets `checkedOut` to false and sets `borrowerId`, `checkedOutAt` and `dueDate` to `null`. `saveBooks` writes every book, and `valueOrBlank` turns each `null` into an empty string. The record therefore keeps its id, title, author and ISBN, with **checkedOut=false and the three loan fields blank**.

- *borrowerId kept as history*: `returnBook` clears it; the app keeps no loan history.
- *Record left out*: `saveBooks` loops over all books whatever their state.
- *Old due date kept*: the due date is cleared along with the other loan fields.

excerpts.quote: this.checkedOut = false; this.borrowerId = null; this.checkedOutAt = null; this.dueDate = null;

notes.title: Why exiting at once still creates both files
notes.body:
`FileStorage.load` begins with `Files.createDirectories(dataDirectory)`, so the folder exists from startup, and missing files load as empty lists. Option 9 calls `saveData`, and `save` calls `saveBooks` and `saveBorrowers`. Each builds a list of lines (empty here) and calls `Files.write`, which creates the file even with no lines. The result is **data/ with two empty files**.

- *Nothing new*: the save does not check whether there is anything to write.
- *Only the folder*: `Files.write` creates each file regardless of how many lines it gets.
- *Startup fails*: missing files are checked with `Files.exists` and treated as empty.

excerpts.quote: Files.createDirectories(dataDirectory);
Files.write(booksFile, lines);
